items.claim: The unit's onset and close both rest on explicit shifts in the text, and the internal koh-amar and the first-person turn are correctly left uncut for lack of any speaker or addressee change.
items.evidence: The feminine second-person imperative opening 10:17 and the turn to direct prayer address to Yahweh at 10:23 are both explicit, textually marked shifts; the koh-amar at 10:18 is joined to 10:17 by a causal because rather than a new speaker, and the first-person lament at 10:19-10:20 and the third-person shepherds' indictment at 10:21 carry no koh-amar, addressee change, or imperative of their own, so holding the whole span as one unit is warranted. The ketiv/qere at 10:17 and the setumah at 10:16, 10:17, 10:18, 10:21, and 10:22 check byte-true against the parashah inventory (single-witness).

items.claim: The onset, internal unity, frame-closing edge, and unit type are all correctly grounded, and the row honestly discloses the confession-voice question rather than silently deciding it.
items.evidence: The turn to direct second-person address to Yahweh at 10:23 is the first such address in the span; the petition-to-imprecation movement across 10:23-10:25 stays in one continuous prayer voice with no new formula or addressee change; the petuchah at 10:25 coincides with the close of the sermon complex that opens at 7:1; and lament_confession is the correct type for a communal petition of this shape. The row leaves the individual-versus-communal speaker question open rather than resolving it, matching the genuine ambiguity in the bytes themselves.

items.claim: The onset correctly identifies a member of the prose-sermon superscription formula class, and the cut before the fresh reintroduction of divine speech at 11:6 is the strongest available seam, correctly defeating the fold-forward alternative.
items.evidence: 11:1 shares its formula shape with 7:1 and opens the covenant-sermon frame at the frame's own byte-anchored boundary; the unit closes on the prophet's own reply, and 11:6 reopens address with a fresh narrative introduction rather than continuing unmarked, which is the real ground for the cut. The petuchah closing the preceding span at 10:25 and the setumah closing this span at 11:5 check byte-true against the inventory; the recurring covenant-words phrasing spanning 11:2 through 11:8 is ordinary sermon vocabulary rather than a formulaic device and does not by itself argue against the cut.

items.claim: The onset at a fresh reintroduction of divine speech carrying its own imperative is a genuine textual seam, and the cut before the second such reintroduction at 11:9 is correctly grounded in a real change of subject rather than mere repetition.
items.evidence: 11:6 reopens address with its own command to proclaim, distinct from the closed exchange of 11:1-11:5; the recap of the fathers' history closes as a discrete report at 11:8; and 11:9 repeats the identical reintroduction formula with a different subject, the present conspiracy rather than the fathers, so both instances are read consistently rather than arbitrarily. The bracketing setumah at 11:5 and 11:8 check byte-true against the inventory and are correctly disclosed as corroboration rather than the driver.

items.claim: The onset correctly reuses the same reintroduction-formula class as the unit before it with a distinct subject, and the internal koh-amar at 11:11 is correctly left uncut because it carries no change of speaker.
items.evidence: 11:9's formula introduces the conspiracy topic distinctly from the fathers'-history recap that precedes it; the koh-amar at 11:11 continues the same reported divine speech already underway with the same speaker, so no cut is warranted there; the unit closes on the altars-indictment climax before a discourse imperative opens fresh address at 11:14. The bracketing and internal setumah at 11:8, 11:10, and 11:13 check byte-true against the inventory.

items.claim: The discourse-imperative onset is correctly grounded, and the addressee turn to a feminine figure from 11:15 is correctly held inside the unit for lack of any formula marking it as its own seam.
items.evidence: The second-person prohibition addressed to the prophet opens the unit at 11:14; the turn to a feminine addressee from 11:15 carries no koh-amar or imperative of its own, and 11:17 is grammatically bound back to the planted-tree image of 11:16, so the four verses read as one unit rather than two. The cut before 11:18 is warranted by that verse's turn to the prophet's own first-person account, a genuine change of scene. The bracketing and internal setumah at 11:13, 11:14, and 11:17 check byte-true against the inventory.

items.claim: The first-person onset is correctly grounded, and the cut before Yahweh's own reply at 11:21 correctly defeats the strongest rival for confession units, folding the petition into its own answering oracle.
items.evidence: The turn to the prophet's own first-person account opens the unit at 11:18 with no verse before it cast in that voice; the petition for vindication continues that voice through 11:20; and the cut before 11:21 is warranted by a koh-amar there that returns the speaker to Yahweh and names specific opponents, a genuine change of who is speaking rather than a continuation of the prophet's own prayer. lament_confession is the correct type for this individual petition. The bracketing setumah at 11:17 and 11:20 check byte-true against the inventory.

items.claim: The onset correctly rests on a real change of speaker back to Yahweh, and the doubled koh-amar clause at 11:22 is correctly held inside the same unit because it carries the same speaker and the same named target forward rather than reopening address.
items.evidence: 11:21's koh-amar names the men of Anathoth as Yahweh resumes speaking immediately after the prophet's own petition closes at 11:20; the second therefore-thus-says-Yahweh clause at 11:22 continues that same speaker and target rather than introducing a new one, so it is correctly read as intensification rather than a fresh unit. The span closes chapter 11 without crossing the frame boundary it sits inside. The bracketing and internal setumah at 11:20, 11:21, and 11:23 check byte-true against the inventory.
